This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company and the claimants respectively under Section 173(1)
of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short), challenging the judgment and award passed in MVC No.153/2010 dated 19.12.2011 by the II Additional District Judge and MACT, Kolar.

The brief facts of the case are that on 11.07.2010, at about 3.10 p.m., when deceased after lunch was on the way to his shop, when he reached near Minarva Circle, Chinthamani, at that time, the driver of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-07-7470 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased, due to which, the deceased fell down and front wheel of NC:
2023:KHC:25507 the Bus ran over the deceased.
The deceased sustained several bleeding injuries and was shifted to Government Hospital, Chinthamani and he succumbed to the injuries on the same day.
Therefore, the claimants have filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.
Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that deceased had also contributed negligence as he was walking carelessly on the busy road.
Therefore, the deceased had also contributed his negligence towards the accident.
Further, quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
Therefore, on these grounds, prays for interference with the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal by allowing the appeal.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants submitted that there is no contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and the income NC: 2023:KHC:25507 taken, the multiplier adopted and also the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on lower side.

Therefore,
prays for enhancement of compensation by allowing the MFA Crob.
6.

The facts revealed from the record are that deceased on 11.07.2010 after having his lunch was on the way to the shop and when he reached near Minarva Circle, Chinthamani, at about after 3.10 p.m., driver of the Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-07-7470 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed the deceased.
Due to which, the deceased fell down and the front wheel of the bus ran over the deceased and the deceased succumbed to the injuries at Government Hospital, Chinthamani on the same day.
Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint and Ex.P.3 is the Mahazar, which shows that the deceased was a pedestrian on the left side of the road and was hit by the bus.

When the accident had occurred at middle of the town, it is the duty of the driver of the bus,
who is driving heavy vehicle to drive in a NC: 2023:KHC:25507 careful manner with all vigilance.
Driving of vehicle in an empty road is different from driving the vehicle within the town limits.
The drivers, who are driving in the middle of the town/city have to be more careful as it is their duty to drive the vehicle in a cautious and careful manner.
If this difference is not borne in the minds of Drivers, then it is nothing but negligence on the part of the drivers.
7. Just because the accident has caused while deceased was crossing the road as a pedestrian, it cannot be said that deceased was negligent while crossing the road.
The driver's task is more onerous.

In the present case, as the driver was driving heavy vehicle, he should have been more Smt. Lakshmikanthamma vs The Senior Manager on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102992467/
4 vigilant, careful and cautious while driving the bus.

sentences.text: Therefore, in this regard, the driver of the bus was completely rash and negligent while driving the vehicle.
Even in the complaint and FIR, entire allegation is made against the driver of the bus.
Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in attributing the entire negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
It is stated that the deceased was running a firm by name 'Sri Rama Coffee Works'.

Exs.P.15 to 17 are the receipts of tax and tax invoices and forms of tax returns filed under the Karnataka Value Added Tax (KVAT) Act, 2003, which shows that the deceased was running a coffee powder business.
The claimants have produced the tax returns showing total turnover of the firm but there is no income tax returns produced showing the income of the deceased.
Under such circumstances, the Tribunal has considered the notional income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- p.m. which is on the lesser side.
The accident is of the year 2010.
Therefore, the notional income of the deceased is Rs.5,500/- p.m. as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

As per principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 25% of income is added towards loss of future prospectus in life.

Therefore, the loss of dependency is hereby re-

Rs.5,500 + Rs.1,375 (25% of Rs.5,500) = Rs.6,875/- Rs.6,875 x 50% x 14 x 12 =
Rs.5,77,500/-
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.5,77,500/- is awarded under the head 'loss of dependency'.
9. The Tribunal has granted a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards 'loss of love and affection'.

As per Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram and Others, reported in 2018 ACJ 2782,
Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded under the head 'loss of love and affection'.

Accordingly, a sum of Rs.88,000/- is awarded under the head 'loss of love and affection'.
10. The Tribunal has granted a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards 'transportation of dead body' and Rs.15,000/- towards 'funeral expenses'.

It is just and reasonable to award a sum of Rs.16,500/-
under the head 'loss of estate' and Rs.16,500/- under the head 'transportation of dead body, funeral expenses, etc'.

The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.4,55,000/-, but the appellants/claimants
are entitled to total compensation of Rs.6,98,500/-.

Therefore, the appellants/claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.2,43,500/- (Rs.4,55,000 - Rs.6,98,500) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
13.
